title: BRICS Parliamentary Forum condemns Pahalgam terror attack, seeks UNSC reforms
syllabus: GS2 › Important international institutions and groupings (BRICS, UN) · GS3 › Terrorism; Linkages between state and non-state actors
summary: The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum in New Delhi adopted a declaration condemning the Pahalgam attack and cross-border terrorism, and calling for UN and Security Council reform.
ideas: Diplomatic gain: BRICS parliaments, including China and Iran, condemned Pahalgam and cross-border terrorism in one text.
At the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum (New Delhi, 2026), members including China and Iran condemned the Pahalgam attack and cross-border terrorism.
India's counter-terror agenda endorsed: zero tolerance, no double standards, no link between terror and religion, and quick adoption of the CCIT.
The BRICS declaration backed India's call for zero tolerance, no double standards and early adoption of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism.
Reform of global governance: BRICS calls for comprehensive UN reform, including the Security Council, and stronger multilateralism.
BRICS parliaments called for comprehensive reform of the UN, including the Security Council, echoing India's long-standing demand.
Parliamentary diplomacy: legislators, not just governments, carry India's positions to other countries.
Hosting the BRICS Parliamentary Forum shows parliamentary diplomacy amplifying India's positions on terror and UN reform.
